Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
1032 AM EDT Sat Oct 3 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Given ongoing radar trends, have bolstered precipitation chances
along/east of U.S. 15 through the early afternoon hours.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) A stalling cold front may bring rain at times through 
  Sunday.

- 2) First widespread frost and freeze potential west of the Blue 
  Ridge early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...A stalling cold front may bring rain at times
through Sunday.

Extensive cloud cover remains over much of the region, although
some cloud breaks are noted along I-70 in north-central
Maryland. The array of nearby radars are showing a band of more
concentrated rain tracking just east of the Blue Ridge toward
the I-95 metros. This will make for a rainy morning amidst the
cool post-frontal air mass. The stable nature of the air mass is
largely limiting hourly amounts to around a trace to 0.05 
inches. The 12Z IAD sounding did show some dry air in the surface
to 900 mb layer. Despite precipitable water values of 1.55
inches, this drier low-level air is eroding some of this
rainfall before reaching the ground. Elsewhere, dry air will 
work into the region from the north and northwest behind the
earlier cold front.

Strong high pressure will pass north of the area today while 
the front stalls just to our south. Southern stream moisture 
will likely overrun the boundary fairly far to the north, but 
there remains some uncertainty in the dividing line between rain
and no rain. The trend has been for a further north track, so 
have shifted rain chances about 20 to 30 miles north with the 
latest forecast package. 

A wave of low pressure will ride along this stalled boundary 
tonight into Sunday, and this may provide a higher chance of 
some heavier rain spreading northward into the area. The Weather
Prediction Center does have our eastern areas in a Marginal 
Excessive Rainfall Outlook, and this seems plausible given the 
potential for a surge of 2"+ PWATs. Rain that does occur will 
likely exit the area Sunday evening.

Being north of the boundary and potentially having a lot of
cloud cover, high temperatures will likely remain in the 60s for
most areas over the weekend.


KEY MESSAGE 2...First widespread frost and freeze potential west of 
the Blue Ridge early next week.

Significant pattern change for the first full week of Oct. CAA 
behind a departing trof will bring the coldest air of the fall thus 
far to the region. A robust area of Canadian high pressure moves 
into the area Mon night through mid-week. Consequently, this is 
forecast to bring a true autumnal feel to the air with daily temps 
well below average. For Tue and Wed, forecast highs will generally 
range from the upper 50s to 60s, with mountain locales mainly in the 
50s. Looking at overnight conditions, the dry nature of the air mass 
allows temperatures to plummet at night. Areas west of the Blue 
Ridge can expect widespread mid/upper 30s on Mon and Tue nights. 
Would not be surprised if some areas just east of the Blue Ridge or 
in northern Maryland have frost as well. This will also include some 
pockets of upper 20s to near the freezing mark. Given the growing 
season continues across the region, there will be a threat of some 
frost/freeze conditions both of those nights. For those with 
sensitive outdoor vegetation, plans should be made to ensure their 
safety in these conditions.

Although Canadian high pressure moves off the coast toward the 
mid/late week period, the overall pattern will remain dry throughout 
next week. Temps slowly rebound through the week as forecast highs 
return to the low/mid 70s. Nighttime lows remain chilly, but the 
threat for frost/freeze conditions should diminish beyond Wed 
morning.

&&

.AVIATION /13Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
A cold front is moving to the south of the area. Light rain
along and north of this boundary is producing a shield of light
rain along the I-95 corridor back to the central Virginia
Piedmont. Given some low-level dry air, there are no
restrictions with this activity at this time.

The front will stall to the south over the weekend, but its
position remains uncertain. Rain chances have increased area-
wide today as the stalled front is trending a bit further 
north. Some heavier rain could move north into most areas by 
Sunday morning as an area of low pressure develops along the 
front. 

Any sub-VFR conditions would likely be limited to CHO today, but
could spread northward Sunday.

VFR conditions early to middle parts of next week. Expect 
NW'ly winds on Mon with gusts around 15 to 20 knots. As high 
pressure crosses the region, winds shift to N'ly by Tue before 
shifting to S-S'ly by mid-week.

&&

.MARINE...
Small Craft Advisories remain in effect for this threat through
early this afternoon.

After that, winds may be relatively lighter until a second cold
front pushes through on Monday.

Behind a cold front, NW'ly winds will increase throughout 
Mon evening into early Tuesday. SCAs are likely going to be needed 
during this uptick in the winds. As Canadian high pressure moves in, 
wind speeds begin to drop off thereafter.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Water levels will be on the decrease as high pressure builds on
the northwest side of the front that continues to push south.

Another tidal surge is possible going into early next week ahead
of the next frontal system. Lots of uncertainty at this time,
but some minor tidal flooding looks possible.

&&
